submitted.rationale: Highest measured EQE (0.0233%) at Cr0.61Sb0.39, slightly above the CrSbO4 stoichiometric point (idx 15, 0.0222%). MACE and MEGNet put the rutile Cr-Sb oxides near the hull (0.06–0.08 eV/atom) with gaps around 1.98 eV, below the 2.1 eV illumination, so they can absorb.

rejected.reason: Sb-rich side measured 0.0103%, merit falls with excess Sb

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile CrSbO4 near-stable (0.065 eV/atom above hull in MACE) with HSE gap ~1.98 eV, just below the 2.1 eV photon energy, so it absorbs. Index 15 (Cr0.48Sb0.52) sits at the CrSbO4 stoichiometry.

Mostly uninformative: Cr3Sb5O16 (Sb-rich ordered model) 0.107 eV/atom above hull, i.e. likely forms as Sb-rich rutile solid solution rather than an ordered phase; its 0.88 eV MEGNet gap is probably an artifact of the ordered mixed-valence model. Measuring index 21 (Cr0.29Sb0.71) to test the Sb-rich rutile region against the stoichiometric point.

Support: Cr-rich Cr5Sb3O16 model is near-stable (0.082 eV/atom above hull) with HSE gap ~1.98 eV (<2.1 eV photon), so it absorbs similarly to CrSbO4. The Sb-rich side measured lower (0.010 vs 0.022%), so the Cr-rich side is the better final test. Index 11 (Cr0.61) matches this composition.
